messages:
claire: FYI ap-southeast1 cohort `ephemeral-gc-fanout` is causing GPU attach delays — ~21 pending.
hugo: seeing long NVMe tails on 5 hosts, %util spikes but low queue depth. dmesg shows nvme admin timeouts on two.
devin: paste dmesg snippet:
```
[ 1023.456789] nvme nvme0: Admin command timeout
[ 1023.457000] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 4096
```
claire: timeline: nightly GC started at 00:05 local and a big autoscaler window at 00:07. looks like GC + provisioning fanout.
storage-bot: ALERT GPU_PROVISIONING_HOLD ap-southeast1: 21 pending at 1768882200
hugo: quick fixes: 1) throttle GC for that label (concurrency=1); 2) taint the 5 noisy nodes `nvme-deg:NoSchedule`; 3) exclude pool from autoscaler for 30m.
devin: applying maintenance flag `storage.gc.concurrency=1` and cordoning noisy nodes now.
claire: after cordon + throttle attach success went from ~40% to ~86%. two drives still have repeated admin timeouts — RMA flagged.
oncall: opened incident INC-2026-4129, notifying hardware and storage teams.
hugo: follow-ups: add alert for nvme admin timeout >1 in 5m, add Grafana panel correlating GC start times with gpu-provisioner pending counts, and require staggered GC windows for future rollouts.
claire: plan: replace 2 drives, re-enable GC in 90m with staggered start and lower concurrency. short spill accepted to protect SLA. :thumbsup:
